title: 국내 여행
intro: 국내 여행은 '좋아하는 여행지 묘사 → 여행 준비 루틴 → 기억에 남는 여행 경험 → 과거와 현재 비교' 순서로 자주 출제됩니다. 친구들과 KTX 타고 간 부산(해운대, 돼지국밥)과 가족과 함께 간 제주 두 가지 이야기만 준비해 두면 거의 모든 질문에 재활용할 수 있습니다. '바쁜 회사 생활과 회의에서 벗어나 쉬는 시간'이라는 직장인 감정 포인트를 꼭 넣으세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Sure, I'd love to talk about ~) → 어디/누구와/어떻게 가는지 기본 정보 → 거기서 하는 일·먹은 음식 세부 → 좋아하는 이유·느낌 → 마무리 문장(So yeah, that's why I really like ~)
여행지는 부산(친구들과, 해운대·돼지국밥)과 제주(대전에 사는 가족과)로 고정해서 묘사·경험·비교 질문에 같은 장면을 돌려 쓰세요.
'금요일 연차 쓰고 2박 3일', 'KTX로 2시간 반'처럼 직장인다운 구체적인 숫자와 장소 이름을 하나씩 넣으면 IH 이상으로 들립니다.
비교 질문은 '대학생 때는 돈이 없어 버스·찜질방 → 지금은 월급으로 KTX·좋은 호텔, 대신 시간이 부족'처럼 과거/현재 시제를 분명히 나눠 말하세요.

expressions.en: Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite place in Korea.
expressions.ko: 네, 제가 한국에서 제일 좋아하는 곳에 대해 말해 볼게요.
expressions.note: 국내 여행 질문의 시작 문장으로 그대로 사용

expressions.en: It takes about two and a half hours by KTX.
expressions.ko: KTX로 두 시간 반 정도 걸려요.

expressions.en: I usually go there with my friends.
I took a day off on Friday.
expressions.note: take a day off: 하루 쉬다(연차 쓰다)

expressions.en: The food was really cheap and delicious.
I pack light, just a small backpack.
expressions.ko: 저는 짐을 가볍게 싸요, 작은 배낭 하나만요.

expressions.en: It was a nice break from work.
It's pretty easy to get there from Seoul.
expressions.ko: 서울에서 거기 가는 건 꽤 쉬워요.

expressions.en: We booked everything on our phones.
Being near the ocean really helps me relax.
expressions.ko: 바다 근처에 있으면 정말 마음이 편해져요.
expressions.note: 동명사 주어 Being ~ 으로 문장을 시작하면 IH 느낌

expressions.en: Back in college, I couldn't afford nice hotels.
expressions.ko: 대학 때는 좋은 호텔에 묵을 여유가 없었어요.
expressions.note: Back in ~ : 예전 ~ 때는 (비교 질문 필수)

expressions.en: The best part was eating pork soup by the sea.
expressions.ko: 제일 좋았던 건 바닷가에서 돼지국밥을 먹은 거예요.

expressions.en: It was one of those trips I'll never forget.
expressions.ko: 절대 잊지 못할 그런 여행 중 하나였어요.

expressions.en: So yeah, that's why I really like traveling in Korea.
expressions.ko: 그래서 제가 국내 여행을 정말 좋아하는 거예요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy traveling within your country. Tell me about a place in Korea that you like to visit. Where is it, what is it like, and why do you like it?
questions.ko: 설문에서 국내 여행을 즐긴다고 하셨습니다. 한국에서 즐겨 찾는 장소에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떤 곳이며, 왜 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 장소 이름·위치·가는 방법 → 거기서 하는 일(해변 산책, 음식) → 좋아하는 이유 → 'So yeah, that's why ~' 마무리
부산 = 친구들, 해운대, 돼지국밥으로 고정하면 경험 질문에서도 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
'바쁜 회사 생활과 회의에서 벗어나 쉰다'는 이유를 넣으면 자연스럽게 감정이 들어갑니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite place in Korea. It's Busan. Busan is a big city by the sea in the south of Korea. It takes about two and a half hours by KTX from Seoul. I usually go there with my friends. We walk along Haeundae Beach and eat pork soup. The food is really cheap and delicious. My job is pretty busy because I have a lot of meetings, so Busan is a nice break from work. So yeah, that's why I really like Busan.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite place in Korea. It's definitely Busan. Busan is the second biggest city in Korea, and it's right next to the ocean. It's pretty easy to get there from Seoul. It only takes about two and a half hours by KTX. I usually go there with my friends from college, maybe once a year. We take a day off on Friday and stay for two nights. When we get there, we walk along Haeundae Beach and sit in a cafe with an ocean view. And of course, we always eat dwaeji gukbap, which is a hot pork soup. It's cheap, but it's so good. Being near the ocean really helps me relax. In Seoul, I'm always sitting in meetings or looking at reports, so the sea feels really fresh to me. So yeah, that's why I really like Busan.
answers.AL: Oh, a place in Korea? Let me think. I'd have to say Busan, hands down. Busan is the second biggest city in Korea, and it's on the southeast coast, so you can see the ocean almost everywhere. It's pretty easy to get there from Seoul. You just hop on the KTX, and about two and a half hours later, you're there. I usually go with a couple of my college friends. We all work now, so we take a day off on Friday and make it a long weekend. Our routine is kind of the same every time. We drop our bags at the hotel, walk along Haeundae Beach, and then grab a big bowl of dwaeji gukbap, which is a hot pork soup that Busan is famous for. Honestly, it tastes way better there than in Seoul. At night, we sit on the beach, listen to the waves, and just talk for hours. What I love most is the feeling of freedom. My life in Seoul is pretty busy because I usually have a lot of meetings, and my phone never stops buzzing. But in Busan, I can finally slow down and breathe. It's like hitting a reset button. So yeah, that's why Busan is my favorite place in Korea.

questions.en: How do you usually plan and prepare for a trip within Korea? Who do you usually travel with, what do you pack, and what do you do before you leave?
questions.ko: 국내 여행을 보통 어떻게 계획하고 준비하나요? 주로 누구와 여행하고, 무엇을 챙기며, 떠나기 전에 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 누구와 가는지 → 계획 순서(연차 신청 → 단톡방 → KTX·숙소 예약) → 짐 싸기 → 'Yeah, that's how ~' 마무리
First, Then, After that, Finally 같은 순서 표현을 쓰면 루틴 답변이 깔끔해져요.
직장인답게 '팀장님께 연차 신청, 떠나기 전 업무 마무리'를 넣으면 페르소나가 살아납니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how I prepare for a trip. I usually travel with my friends. First, I ask my team leader for a day off. Then, my friends and I make a group chat and pick a place. After that, we book KTX tickets and a hotel on our phones. I pack light, just a small backpack. I bring clothes, a phone charger, and my earphones. The night before, I finish all my work. Yeah, that's how I usually prepare for a trip.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about how I prepare for a trip in Korea. I usually travel with two or three friends from college. Since we all work, the hardest part is finding a date. So first, we make a group chat and pick a weekend that works for everyone. Then I ask my team leader for a day off, usually on a Friday. After that, we book everything on our phones. KTX tickets go fast, so we book them about a month early. We also look for a hotel near the beach or the downtown area. I pack light, just a small backpack with some clothes, a charger, and my earphones for the train. Before I leave, I make sure to finish my reports so nobody calls me during the trip. Yeah, that's how I usually get ready for a trip.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about how I prepare for a trip. To be honest, planning a trip as an office worker is a lot different from when I was a student. I usually travel with a few close friends from college, and since we all have jobs now, the trickiest part is just finding a weekend that works for everyone. So the first thing we do is make a group chat and throw out some dates. Once we agree, I ask my team leader for a day off, usually on a Friday, so we can turn it into a long weekend. After that, we split up the work. One friend books the KTX tickets, another one finds a hotel, and I'm usually in charge of finding good places to eat, because I'm kind of a foodie. When it comes to packing, I pack light. I just bring a small backpack with a couple of outfits, a phone charger, and my earphones, because listening to music on the train is part of the fun. The night before I leave, I wrap up all my work and set an out-of-office message, so I don't have to check my email on the beach. Yeah, that's pretty much how I prepare for a trip in Korea.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable trip you took in Korea. When was it, where did you go, who were you with, and what happened that made it so memorable?
questions.ko: 국내에서 다녀온 기억에 남는 여행에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제, 어디로, 누구와 갔으며, 어떤 일이 있어서 그렇게 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디·누구와 → 무슨 일이 있었는지(시간 순서) → 그때 느낀 감정 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
제주 가족 여행처럼 '혼자 사는 직장인이 오랜만에 가족과 보낸 시간'이라는 감정 포인트가 있으면 기억에 남는 이유가 분명해집니다.
과거 시제(went, rented, saw)를 끝까지 일관되게 쓰세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about a memorable trip. Last fall, I went to Jeju Island with my family. My family lives in Daejeon, and I live alone in Seoul, so I don't see them very often. We rented a car and drove around the island. We saw the beautiful ocean and ate black pork. My younger brother Junho took a lot of funny pictures. It was really nice to spend time with my family. Yeah, that's my most memorable trip in Korea.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about a memorable trip I took in Korea. It was last fall, and I went to Jeju Island with my family. My parents and my younger brother Junho live in Daejeon, and I live alone in Seoul because of my job, so we don't get to see each other much. That's why this trip was so special. We flew there from Gimpo and rented a car. My dad drove, and we went around the island for three days. We visited a beautiful beach, climbed a small mountain, and ate black pork, which Jeju is famous for. The best part was the last night. We sat on the hotel balcony and talked for hours, just like when I lived at home. I realized how much I missed them. Yeah, that's why it was such a memorable trip for me.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable trip? Let me think. I'd say it was the trip I took to Jeju Island with my family last fall. Ever since I moved to Seoul for my job, I've been living alone, and my parents and my younger brother Junho are still in Daejeon. So honestly, we only see each other on holidays, and even then it's just for a day or two. My mom had been saying for a while that she wanted a family trip, so I finally took a few days off and booked everything. We flew to Jeju, rented a car, and drove around the island for three days. We walked along the beach, climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong early in the morning to watch the sunrise, and ate way too much black pork. Junho kept taking silly photos of my dad, and we couldn't stop laughing. But what really made it memorable happened on the last night. We were sitting on the hotel balcony, and my dad said he was really proud of me for living on my own and working hard. I almost cried. It was one of those trips I'll never forget, because it reminded me how lucky I am to have them. Yeah, that's my most memorable trip in Korea.

questions.en: How has the way you travel in Korea changed over the years? Compare the trips you took when you were younger with the trips you take now.
questions.ko: 국내 여행하는 방식이 몇 년 사이에 어떻게 달라졌나요? 어렸을 때(예전에) 다녀온 여행과 요즘 다니는 여행을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 예전 여행(대학생 때: 돈 없음, 버스, 저렴한 숙소) → 지금 여행(직장인: KTX, 좋은 호텔, 연차) → 무엇이 더 좋은지·느낌 → 마무리 문장
Back in college / These days 로 과거와 현재를 확실히 나누고 시제를 맞추세요.
'돈은 생겼지만 시간이 없다'처럼 장단점을 하나씩 말하면 비교가 깊어 보입니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how my trips have changed. Back in college, I didn't have much money. So my friends and I took the bus and stayed in cheap guesthouses. We traveled for a long time during vacation. These days, I work at an IT company, so I have more money. I take the KTX and stay in nice hotels. But I don't have much time, so my trips are short. Yeah, that's how my trips have changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about how my trips in Korea have changed. Back in college, I didn't have much money, so my trips were really simple. My friends and I took the bus because it was cheaper than the KTX, and we usually stayed in small guesthouses or even jjimjilbangs. But we had long vacations, so we could travel for a week. These days, things are pretty different. I work at an IT company now, so I can afford to take the KTX and stay in a nice hotel. We also eat at better restaurants. The downside is that I don't have much time. I can only take a day or two off, so most of my trips are just long weekends. To be honest, I miss the long trips, but I really enjoy being comfortable now. Yeah, that's how my trips have changed over the years.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a good question. Let me think. My trips have changed a lot, mostly because I went from being a broke college student to an office worker. Back in college, I had tons of free time but almost no money. My friends and I would take the cheapest night bus, sleep in jjimjilbangs, and live on convenience store kimbap for days. It sounds kind of rough, but honestly, we had a blast. We could travel for a whole week during vacation and never worry about anything. These days, it's pretty much the opposite. Now that I work at an IT company, I have a steady paycheck, so I can afford to take the KTX and stay in a hotel with an ocean view. We eat at nice restaurants instead of counting every won. But the catch is time. I usually have a lot of meetings, so I can only take a day or two off, and most of my trips are just long weekends. Sometimes I even check my work messages on the train, which I really hate. If I had to choose, I'd say I like traveling now because it's so much more comfortable. But I do miss that carefree feeling. So yeah, that's how my trips in Korea have changed.

pronunciation.tip: '비-치'처럼 '이' 소리를 길게 늘이세요. 짧게 말하면 전혀 다른 단어로 들릴 수 있어요.
첫 음절 '메'에 강세. '메머러블'처럼 뒤는 약하게 흘려요.
'컴프터블' 세 음절처럼 말해요. 'com-for-ta-ble'로 또박또박 끊지 마세요.
